title: expansion-tracker status vocabulary drift: analyst.md writes 'ready-for-integration', decider.md Priority 4 filter only matches 'complete' || 'revised'. 75+ days of silent integration blockage. Design a durable fix (widen decider filter, normalize analyst vocab, or add integrity check — operator's choice, small directive).

context.why_now: Operator investigation 2026-07-12 (following morning check-in on the external Claude review EXPs stuck at ready-for-integration for 6+ days) found the root cause: decider's Priority 4 filter at decider.md:248 checks (i.status === 'complete' || i.status === 'revised') && !i.integrated. Analyst.md line 287 explicitly documents 'ready-for-integration' as a valid status (with a 2026-04-27-vintage 'tracker-staleness fallback' comment), but decider was never updated to accept it. Result: 75+ days of silent integration drift. EXP-626 (from 2026-04-27) is the oldest surviving witness — sitting at ready-for-integration since the day the vocabulary was introduced.

the_smoking_gun.decider_filter: decider.md:248 — node -e "const t=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('monitor/analyst/expansion-tracker.json','utf8'));const c=t.items.filter(i=>(i.status==='complete'||i.status==='revised')&&!i.integrated);console.log(c.length?'EXPANSIONS: '+c.length+' ready to integrate':'NO PENDING EXPANSIONS')"
the_smoking_gun.analyst_documentation: analyst.md:287 — 'if status: "ready-for-integration" BUT the EXP's content can be cross-checked... Tracker-staleness fallback (added 2026-04-27 per analyst report)'
the_smoking_gun.current_tracker_state: 5 items stuck at ready-for-integration: EXP-626 (build-scripts/generate-html.js 4-cluster generalization, from 2026-04-27), EXP-650/651/652/653 (external Claude review commissions from 2026-07-05/06)
the_smoking_gun.why_it_took_75_days_to_notice: EXPs at ready-for-integration accumulate silently; decider prints 'NO PENDING EXPANSIONS' when its filter matches nothing. Cross-prompt vocabulary drift has no automated check. Nobody caught it until this morning's report from operator on the specific external-review commissions.

context.immediate_state: Operator flipped EXP-650/651/652/653 to status='complete' in the same commit that files this directive. Decider's next 02:07 UTC run will integrate them. EXP-626 NOT flipped — needs content cross-check against current build-scripts/generate-html.js first (may be OBE-integrated but tracker-stale, may be legitimate 75-day backlog). Operator will decide on EXP-626 after tinker recommends the durable vocabulary fix.

options_to_evaluate.label: Widen decider Priority 4 filter to accept 'ready-for-integration' alongside 'complete' and 'revised'
options_to_evaluate.shape: One-line change to decider.md:248 filter. Preserves analyst's existing vocabulary without asking analyst to change.
options_to_evaluate.cost: Minimal. Single string edit in a prompt.
options_to_evaluate.risk: Very low. Filter widening never blocks legitimate items; if a status shouldn't-be-integrable slips in, that's a separate schema-integrity check's job.
options_to_evaluate.downstream_effect: EXP-626 gets integrated on decider's next run (assuming Q4 filter widening lands before EXP-626's operator investigation, need to be handled).

options_to_evaluate.label: Normalize analyst.md (and analyst-baby.md) to write 'complete' instead of 'ready-for-integration'
options_to_evaluate.shape: Update analyst prompt(s) so future EXPs use the older vocabulary. Retroactively flip existing ready-for-integration items in expansion-tracker.json to complete.
options_to_evaluate.cost: Small. Prompt edit + a one-shot tracker sweep.
options_to_evaluate.risk: Analyst prompt has other references to ready-for-integration (the tracker-staleness fallback comment) that would need updating.
options_to_evaluate.downstream_effect: Preserves decider's existing filter; commits the analyst to the older vocabulary.

options_to_evaluate.label: Add integrity vocabulary-drift check across prompts (broader class fix)
options_to_evaluate.shape: New integrity Section 9e: parse enum-value references across analyst/decider/curmudgeon/etc. prompts and flag any status vocabulary used by one prompt that is not accepted by any consumer. Would have caught this in ~1 day instead of 75.
options_to_evaluate.cost: Moderate. Not just this bug — needs a small parser for prompt-referenced status enums.
options_to_evaluate.risk: Prompts aren't machine-readable in a strict sense, so the parser needs heuristics; false positives possible.
options_to_evaluate.downstream_effect: Catches similar drifts across other multi-prompt schemas (issue status, EXP status, review class, priority tiers, etc.). Bigger scope than this one bug but might be the honest fix if we care about the class.

options_to_evaluate.label: OPT-1 + OPT-3 combined
options_to_evaluate.shape: Ship the small filter widening AND the integrity drift check. Belt + suspenders.

If tinker recommends OPT-1 alone (cheapest fix), that's fine. If recommendation is OPT-3 or OPT-4, must justify why the broader-class investigation is worth the effort vs. just fixing this one drift.
part_B_recommendation.output: One-paragraph recommendation at the top of the design report.

part_C_ship_or_follow_up.if_larger_option: OPT-3 or OPT-4 requires new script + integrity prompt edit — author as PROP, propose-only, operator ratifies next session.
